description_en: The temple is located within the religious complex of Dhuleśvara, on a hill 3,5 km north of Dullu.The site of Dhuleśvara is part of an area know as Pañcakośī. The sites of the Pañcakośī are visited by pilgrims from all over western Nepal. The sites are notorious for their flame temples (natural gas flames), said to mark places where Satī's body parts fell while Śiva carried her charred body (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). While parts like the Satī's head (sirā) fell in Sīrasthān (DLK0130), the rest of the body, reduced to dust (dhūli), fell in Dhuleśvara.The temple is built on the model of Newar temples with multiple roofs and a peristyle. It is built with bricks and mud mortar. The door is facing west. The monument was rebuilt in the 19th century by Colonel Kulman Singh Basnyāt (Sharma 2012, p. 94).Inside the sanctum is a square pit where ashes and a light breeze can sometimes come forth. A stone stele of Śiva and Pārvatī (DLK0331-001) was installed inside the sanctum, in front of the pit. It was not on site when assessed in 2014 and 2022. The statue was estimated by D. R. Sharma to date from the 13th century (Sharma 2012, p. 95).
